text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Credit Foncier de France holds extraordinary shareholders meeting today to vote on technical change in statute allowing the property lender extra time to reconstitute its capital while negotiations with the government over the bank's future continue. Staff may also call off three-week old occupation at company's headquarters.
-- EDF utility considers closing nine out of 50 fuel and coal-powered electricity plants in 1997 due to current overcapacity and upcoming opening of two nuclear plants.
-- Civil service unions call strike for March 6 as government refuses a wage adjustment to compensate a 1996 freeze.
-- Pension funds to be offered to some 14 million private sector workers after National Assembly and Senate committee approve final draft this morning.
-- State-owned savings bank Caisse d'Epargne to offer home and automobile insurance contracts through a partnership with Mutuelles du Mans.
-- Generale des Eaux to transfer to Havas its stake in pay-TV channel Canal Plus, but also its loss-making subsidiary Generale d'Images, and a few other assets.
-- Government to grant civil servants a one percent wage rise for 1997.
-- Government may include loss-making Giat Industries arms manufacturer on the list of firms to be privatised, in order to allow it to enter into European partnerships.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe confirms he sees France making the 2.3 percent government growth target for 1997.

-- Credit Martiniquais, one of three banks in French overseas territory Martinique, estimated to hold some 500- billion-franc worth of doubtful debt, compared to an operating profit of 70 million francs in 1995.
